applicant.name: Dr. Matteo Bianchi
applicant.organisation: Department of Neurosciences, University of Padua (university research group)

purpose: For a teaching and research project on secondary prevention after ischaemic stroke, access to individual-level patient data is essential to us. We want to examine statin and anticoagulant use across age groups.
question: How often are statins and direct oral anticoagulants used for ischaemic stroke in different age groups?
definitions: Adult = aged 18 or older on 31 December 2025.
Ischaemic stroke = any condition with an ICD-10 code starting with I63.
Statin = ATC code starting with C10AA; Direct oral anticoagulant = ATC code starting with B01AF.
A medication is active on 31 December 2025 if start_date is on or before that day and end_date is empty or on or after that day.
Report per band: adults with ischaemic stroke, % with an active statin, % with an active direct oral anticoagulant, one decimal.

expected.reason: The purpose is allowed (Art. 53). The application does not show why anonymised statistics are not enough, so pseudonymised records are not justified (Art. 66(2)). It is answered with anonymised statistics instead (Art. 68(3), Art. 69).

judge.why: Rule 5: calling individual data essential is not an explanation of what records allow that statistics cannot, and the report definition is percentages per age band, so Rule 4 fails and the access application defaults to statistics.
